title: Draft a Lessons Learned Summary
description: Identify root causes and create SMART action items from a scenario.
problemStatement:
Read the following scenario from a Lessons Learned meeting:

*'During the ransomware incident, the security team tried to contact the backup administrator to verify tape inventory. The on-call list had an old phone number. It took 3 hours to find the correct person. By the time they verified the backups, the ransomware had already encrypted the online backup repository.'*

**Task:**
1. Use the 'Five Whys' technique (or root cause analysis) to identify the **root cause**.
2. Create **two SMART Action Items** to prevent this from happening again.

**Output Format:**
```
Root Cause: [Brief statement]

Action Item 1: [SMART description]
Action Item 2: [SMART description]
```
hints: Think about why the phone number was old (process failure).
Think about why the online backup was accessible to ransomware (technical failure).
Action items need Owners and Due Dates.
expectedOutput:
Root Cause: Lack of automated on-call scheduling and failure to enforce immutable backup storage (3-2-1 rule).

Action Item 1: Implement PagerDuty (or similar) for automated on-call rotations and contact updates. Owner: IT Operations Manager. Due: June 30, 2026.
Action Item 2: Configure immutable object lock on the cloud backup repository to prevent deletion/encryption by ransomware. Owner: Backup Administrator. Due: May 15, 2026.
solutionCode:
Root Cause: Inadequate process for maintaining emergency contact information and insufficient backup isolation (lack of air-gap/immutability).

Action Item 1: Implement an automated on-call management platform (e.g., PagerDuty, Opsgenie) integrated with the corporate directory. Owner: IT Service Management Lead. Due: June 30, 2026.
Action Item 2: Enable S3 Object Lock (or equivalent) with Compliance Mode on all backup repositories to ensure backups cannot be deleted or encrypted by ransomware. Owner: Cloud Infrastructure Team. Due: May 30, 2026.
